He played [[college basketball]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]]. White was a top high school player in [[North Carolina]], finishing his career as the top prep scorer in state history. After being selected by the [[Chicago Bulls]] in the first round of the [[2019 NBA draft]] with the seventh overall pick, he was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] in 2020. In 2024, White finished second in [[NBA Most Improved Player]] award behind [[Tyrese Maxey]]. ==High school career== White, a 6'4" [[combo guard]], played high school basketball at the Greenfield School in [[Wilson, North Carolina]]. He scored 3,573 points over his four-year career, becoming the all-time leading scorer in North Carolina high school basketball history, a record previously held by [[JamesOn Curry]].{{cite web |last1 = Blake | first1 = J. Mike |last2 = Pope IV | first2 = Jonas| title=UNC basketball recruit becomes NC's all-time scoring leader, but where will the record go? |url=https://www.newsobserver.com/sports/high-school/article197044374.html |work=[[The News & Observer]] |access-date=November 9, 2018 |date=January 27, 2018}}{{cite web |last=Martin |first=Ross |title=Coby White Concludes Prep Career With N.C. Record 3,573 Points |url=https://247sports.com/college/north-carolina/article/unc-tar-heels-coby-white-concludes-prep-career-with-nc-record-3573-points-115585022/ |work=[[247Sports.com]] |access-date=November 9, 2018 |date=February 27, 2018 }} He was named [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards#State winners|North Carolina Gatorade Player of the Year]] in both his junior and senior seasons.{{Cite web |title=North Carolina Gatorade Player of the Year Awards |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/highschool/awards/1/80 |access-date=December 23, 2025 |website=basketball.realgm.com |language=en}} At the close of his senior season, White was named [[North Carolina Mr. Basketball]] as the state's top high school player.{{cite web |last = Wertz Jr. | first = Langston | title=UNC, Duke recruits named Mr. Basketball in North, South Carolina |url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/high-school/article207586694.html |work=[[The Charlotte Observer]] |access-date=November 9, 2018 |date=March 31, 2018}} White was also awarded the 2018 ''USA Today's'' North Carolina Player of the Year.{{Cite web|url=https://www.usab.com:443/basketball/players/mens/w/white-coby.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181109234735/https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/w/white-coby.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 9, 2018|title=Coby White|website=usab.com|language=en-US|access-date=July 31, 2019}} He was named to the [[2018 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2018 McDonald's All-American Game]] alongside fellow UNC signee [[Nassir Little]].{{cite web |last = Lindsay | first = Michael | title=White one of two Tar Heels in McDonalds All-American Game |url=http://www.wilsontimes.com/stories/white-one-of-two-tar-heels-in-mcdonalds-all-american-game,119202 |work=[[The Wilson Times]] |access-date=November 9, 2018 |date=March 27, 2018}} White also was nominated to the [[MaxPreps]] All-America first team. During the summer after graduating, White was named to the United States U18 National team to compete in the [[2018 FIBA Under-18 Americas Championship]] in Canada.{{cite web | title=Goldsboro native, future Tar Heel Coby White named to U18 national team |url=https://www.wralsportsfan.com/goldsboro-native-future-tar-heel-coby-white-named-to-u18-national-team/17606830/ |work=[[The Wilson Times]] |access-date=November 9, 2018 |date=June 5, 2018}} White helped lead the team to a gold medal as the team's top scorer, earning all-tournament honors.{{cite web | title=White earns all-tournament honors as U.S. U18 team downs Canada for gold|url=https://goheels.com/news/2018/6/17/mens-basketball-white-earns-all-tournament-honors-as-us-u18-team-downs-canada-for-gold.aspx |work=GoHeels.com White also broke a North Carolina basketball freshman record of three point shooting, hitting 82 during his college season. On April 3, 2019, White declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]] after one season at North Carolina, where he earned All-ACC 2nd Team honors.{{cite web |last1=Rapp |first1=Timothy |title=Coby White |website=bleacherreport.com |access-date= April 3, 2019 |date=April 3, 2019 |quote=North Carolina freshman guard Coby White announced Wednesday he is entering the 2019 NBA draft}} ==Professional career== ===Chicago Bulls (2019–2026)=== On June 20, 2019, the [[Chicago Bulls]] drafted Coby White with the seventh overall pick in the [[2019 NBA draft]].{{cite web |title= Coby White drafted seventh overall by the Chicago Bulls in the NBA Draft |url=https://www.tarheelblog.com/2019/6/20/18692372/coby-white-nba-draft-chicago-bulls-results-unc-basketball |publisher= SB Nation |access-date= June 20, 2019}} White is the first player from North Carolina to be drafted in the first round by the Bulls since [[Michael Jordan]] in 1984.{{cite web |title= Bulls hope selection of North Carolina's Coby White with No. 7 pick in NBA draft will solve their point guard problem: 'I've been competing all my life' |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/bulls/ct-bulls-nba-draft-coby-white-20190621-iernovgxfrg4xaznk4ymeazq2q-story.html |work= Chicago Tribune |access-date= June 21, 2019}} On July 1, White signed with the Bulls.{{cite web |title=Bulls Sign Coby White |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/bulls-sign-coby-white |publisher=National Basketball Association |access-date=July 1, 2019}} White participated in the [[2019 NBA Summer League]] with fellow 2019 draftee [[Daniel Gafford]], where he averaged 15.0 points, 5.6 rebounds, and 4.8 assists per game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.bleachernation.com/bulls/2019/07/15/coby-whites-summer-league-performance-was-a-mostly-positive-mixed-bag/|title=Coby White's Summer League Performance Was a (Mostly Positive) Mixed Bag|website=bleachernation.com|access-date=July 25, 2019}} On October 23, White made his debut in the NBA, coming off the bench in a 126–125 loss to the [[2019–20 Charlotte Hornets season|Charlotte Hornets]] with 17 points, three rebounds and seven assists.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160625|title=Hornets rookie Washington nets 27 in 126-125 win over Bulls|date=October 23, 2019|publisher=ESPN|access-date=October 23, 2019}} This game made him the first player born in the 2000s to play in the NBA. On November 12, 2019, White hit seven 3-pointers in the fourth quarter against the [[2019–20 New York Knicks season|New York Knicks]], setting a Bulls franchise record for most 3-pointers made in a single quarter, and finished with 27 points in the 120–102 victory.{{cite news |last=Owens |first=Jason |title=Bulls rookie Coby White outscores Knicks in 4th quarter with record 3-point barrage |work=[[Yahoo Sports]] |date=November 12, 2019 |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/bulls-rookie-coby-white-outscores-knicks-in-4th-quarter-with-record-3-point-barrage-044727108.html |access-date=November 13, 2019}} On February 22, 2020, White scored a then career-high 33 points in a 112–104 loss to the [[Phoenix Suns]]. White would match that career high the next day, leading the Bulls to a 126–117 win over the [[Washington Wizards]]. White became the first rookie in NBA history with consecutive 30-point games off the bench.{{cite web |title= Coby White made NBA history and Zach LaVine set a team 3-point record: 3 takeaways from the Bulls' 126-117 win over the Wizards |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/bulls/ct-chicago-bulls-wizards-coby-white-20200224-j25z6rdzzvaa7p73pvelo2xuki-story.html |work=Chicago Tribune |access-date= April 25, 2020}} On February 25, White continued the streak and exceeded his career-high, scoring 35 points in a 124–122 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web | last=Kaskey-Blomain | first=Michael | title=Coby White makes NBA history by becoming first rookie reserve to score 30-plus in three straight games | website=CBS Sports | date=2020-02-26 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/coby-white-makes-nba-history-by-becoming-first-rookie-reserve-to-score-30-plus-in-three-straight-games/ | access-date=2025-12-09}} On September 15, 2020, White was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|2019–20 NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] by the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2020/09/15/nba-2019-20-all-rookie-first-team-official-release|title=Ja Morant, Zion Williamsom headline 2019-20 Kia All-Rookie First Team Tyler Herro, Rui Hachimura voted to Second Team|date=September 15, 2020|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=September 15, 2020}} On February 10, 2021, White finished with 30 points, eight 3-pointers, and 7 assists in a 129–116 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]], setting a Bulls franchise record with teammate [[Zach LaVine]] when they each made 8 shots from behind the arc.{{cite web |title= How Zach LaVine and Coby White made 3-point history in Bulls' win over Pelicans | url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/how-zach-lavine-and-coby-white-made-3-point-history-in-bulls-win-over-pelicans/ |work= CBS Sports | access-date= February 11, 2021}} On June 10, 2021, White underwent left shoulder surgery and was ruled out for at least four months.{{Cite web |title=White undergoes shoulder surgery, to be evaluated in 4 months |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/chicago/bulls/coby-white-undergoes-shoulder-surgery-be-evaluated-4-months |access-date=May 10, 2022 |website=NBC Sports}} On September 22, the Bulls exercised their fourth-year option on White, keeping him under team control through the 2022–23 season.{{Cite web|last=BuzzOnTap|date=2021-09-22|title=Bulls Exercise Options on Coby White and Patrick Willams|url=https://ontapsportsnet.com/2021/09/22/chicago-bulls-exercise-options-coby-white-patrick-willams/|access-date=2021-09-22|website=On Tap Sports Net|language=en-US}} On January 31, 2023, in a 108–103 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], White became the fastest player (237 games) in Bulls franchise history to make 500 career three-point baskets.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/chuck-checks-in-02-01-23|title=Chuck Checks In - 02.01.23|publisher=National Basketball Association|accessdate=March 26, 2023}} On July 7, 2023, White signed a three-year, $36 million contract extension with the Bulls.{{cite web|url=https://bullswire.usatoday.com/2023/07/01/chicago-bulls-nba-free-agency-coby-white-contract-extension-good-deal/|title=Bulls praised for Coby White extension: 'Got him on a good deal'|website=USA Today|last=Simone|first=Jack|date=July 1, 2023|access-date=April 18, 2024}} On April 17, 2024, White scored a then career-high 42 points in a 131–116 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in the [[NBA play-in tournament|play-in tournament]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/bulls-news-coby-white-demar-derozan-break-down-play-in-win-vs-hawks|title=Coby White, DeMar DeRozan break down crazy Bulls play-in win vs. Hawks|website=ClutchPoints|last=White|first=Scotty|date=April 17, 2024|access-date=April 17, 2024}} It was the second-most in play-in tournament history behind [[Jayson Tatum]]’s 50 points game in [[2021 NBA play-in tournament|2021]]. On April 23, 2024, White finished second in the race for [[2023–24 NBA season|2023–24]] [[NBA Most Improved Player Award|NBA Most Improved Player]], losing narrowly to Philadelphia's [[Tyrese Maxey]].{{Cite web|title=76ers' Tyrese Maxey Wins 2023-24 NBA Most Improved Player of the Year Award|url= https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10116715-76ers-tyrese-maxey-wins-2023-24-nba-most-improved-player-of-the-year-award|date=April 23, 2024 |website=bleacherreport.com|access-date=April 23, 2024}} On January 4, 2025, White scored 33 points and a career-high nine three-pointers in a 139–126 win against the [[New York Knicks]].{{Cite web|title=White nails career-high nine 3s, scores 33 as Bulls beat Knicks 139-126 after honoring Rose |url=https://wgntv.com/sports/bulls/white-nails-career-high-nine-3s-scores-33-as-bulls-beat-knicks-139-126-after-honoring-rose |date=January 4, 2025 |website=WGNTV.com|access-date=January 4, 2025}} On March 6, White scored a career-high 44 points in a 125–123 victory over the [[Orlando Magic]].{{Cite web |last=Cowley |first=Joe |date=March 6, 2025 |title=No Magic against Coby White as the Bulls guard goes off for 44 in a win |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/bulls/2025/03/06/no-magic-coby-white-bulls-guard-goes-off-44-in-a-win |access-date=March 6, 2025 |website=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]}} On March 17, he was awarded Eastern Conference [[NBA Player of the Month and Week|Player of the Week]] for the first time in his career after averaging 27.0 PPG for three games.{{Cite web|date=March 17, 2025 |title=Coby White Named Eastern Conference Player of the Week |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/coby-white-named-eastern-conference-player-of-the-week |access-date=March 21, 2025 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} Three days later, White scored 35 points in a 128–116 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{Cite web|date=March 21, 2025 |title=Coby White-led Bulls rally from 19 down to beat Kings |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/basketball/coby-white-led-bulls-rally-19-down-beat-kings-2025-03-21/ |access-date=March 21, 2025 |work=Field Level Media|publisher=Reuters}} On March 22, White put up 36 points in a 146–115 win against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{Cite web|date=March 23, 2025 |title=LeBron James' return from injury spoiled by Bulls' phenomenal effort in 146-115 win over Lakers |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401705594 |access-date=March 24, 2025 |agency=Associated Press|publisher=ESPN}} On March 24, he was awarded his second career Player of the Week. He became the second Bulls player to win the award in back-to-back weeks, following [[Michael Jordan]].{{Cite web|date=March 24, 2025 |title=Coby White named Eastern Conference Player of the Week |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/coby-white-named-eastern-conference-player-of-the-week-2 |access-date=March 24, 2025 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} On April 1, he was awarded his first Player Of the Month award. He became the sixth Bull to earn the award, joining Jordan, Pippen, Rose, Butler, and DeRozan.{{Cite web|date=April 1, 2025 |title=Coby White selected as KIA NBA Player of the Month in the East Player of the Week |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/coby-white-selected-as-kia-nba-player-of-the-month-in-the-east |access-date=April 1, 2025 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} White made 74 appearances (73 starts) for the Bulls during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 20.4 points, 3.7 rebounds, and 4.5 assists.{{Cite web|title=Coby White 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4395651/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=May 10, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} White played in 29 games (including 26 starts) for Chicago in the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], recording averages of 18.6 points, 3.7 rebounds, and 4.7 assists.{{Cite web|title=Coby White 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4395651/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=May 10, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} === Charlotte Hornets (2026–present) === On February 4, 2026, White and [[Mike Conley Jr.]] were traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in exchange for [[Ousmane Dieng]], [[Collin Sexton]] and multiple second-round draft picks.{{Cite web |title=Hornets Acquire Coby White And Mike Conley From Bulls {{!}} Charlotte Hornets |url=https://hornets.com/news/hornets-acquire-coby-white-and-mike-conley-from-bulls |access-date=2026-02-05 |website=hornets.com |language=en}} On February 24, he made his debut for the Hornets in a 131–99 win against the [[2025–26 Chicago Bulls season|Chicago Bulls]].{{cite news|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2026/02/24/chicago-bulls-charlotte-hornets-coby-white-debut/|title=Chicago Bulls lose 131-99 to the Charlotte Hornets in Coby White’s debut for his new team|first=Matt|last=Carlson|date=February 24, 2026|accessdate=March 1, 2026|website=Chicago Tribune}} In 21 appearances for Charlotte, White averaged 15.6 points, 3.0 rebounds, and 3.0 assists. On July 6, 2026, White re-signed with the Hornets on a three-year, $74 million contract.{{Cite web|title=Sources: Coby White to re-sign with Hornets on 3-year, $74M deal|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49176539/sources-coby-white-re-sign-hornets-3-year-74m-deal|access-date=June 30, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en|date=June 25,
